newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to join central European trade bloc.
newsitem.headline: Romania to join central European trade bloc.

text.p: Romania signed the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) on Saturday and will become a member of the bloc in July.
"This agreement will allow Romania's access to a market of 90 million people without trade barriers," Industry Ministry Calin Tariceanu said after the signing ceremony in Bucharest.
On July 1, Romania will become the sixth member of CEFTA, which now includes the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.

Bucharest sees CEFTA membership as a key step in its attempts to join the European Union, alongside its efforts to carry out the legal and structural adjustments needed to get in line for a possible EU entry as well as to implement an ambitious reform programme.
Bulgaria, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Ukraine are also seeking CEFTA membership.

CEFTA promotes harmonised economic development among member countries through expansion of trade. Its original goal was to set up a free trade zone by 2001. It was set up in 1992 by Hungary, Poland and ex-Czechoslovakia as a European Union-type grouping to replace the communist-era trading bloc Comecon.
